spec.description: "Dead Man's Switch": protects against network malfunction, extreme latency, or unexpected matching-engine downtime by starting a countdown timer in the trading engine that cancels all account orders on expiry. The client must keep sending requests to push back the trigger time, or send `timeout: 0` to disable the mechanism. Once the timer expires, all orders are cancelled and the feature stays disabled until the next request. Recommended use: a call every 15-30 seconds with `timeout: 60`. It is also recommended to disable the timer ahead of scheduled trading-engine maintenance, since a still-armed timer cancels all orders when the engine returns from downtime.

request.title: CancelAllOrdersAfterParams
request.description: Parameters for the dead man's switch: resets/extends the countdown timer that cancels all account orders on expiry.

timeout.description: Duration in seconds to set/extend the timer; should be less than 86400 seconds. A timeout of `0` disables the mechanism.

currentTime.description: RFC3339 engine time at which the request was received.

triggerTime.description: RFC3339 time after which all orders will be cancelled, unless the timer is extended or disabled first.

notes: `token` (the auth bearer token) is documented by Kraken as a required params field but is deliberately absent from this schema: `core/transport/ws.py`'s `SocketConnection.rpc_send` merges the cached token into every outgoing `params` on the private connection -- trading calls and subscribe/unsubscribe alike -- so it is transport-injected, never a caller-supplied argument, the same way `req_id` (the declared `correlate` field) never appears in a requestBody schema. The doc page's URL slug is `cancel_after` (`/spot-websocket-v2/cancel_after`) and its title is "Cancel on Disconnect", but the wire `method` value shown in the request/response tabs and every JSON example on that page is `cancel_all_orders_after` -- confirmed from the fetched page, matching discovery.md's surface list and core.md's trading-method list. `channel` (and the directory/function name) uses the wire name, not the URL slug; `docs` still points at the `cancel_after` page since that is the URL that actually resolves.
